intro: Describe the diagram in Mermaid-like text. Rhumb draws it as a block diagram that follows the selected standard.

start.title: Quick start
start.text: A diagram is plain text. Rhumb redraws it as you type; an error message tells you which line to fix.

steps.header: Start with flowchart TD (or LR for a wide diagram).
steps.blocks: Give every block an identifier and a form, text in quotes: check{"x > 0?"}.
steps.lines: Join blocks with arrows: A --> B --> C.
steps.branches: Label the branches of a decision: A -->|Yes| B.
steps.export: Pick the standard on the Config tab, then export SVG or PNG with the Actions buttons.

structure.title: Text rules
structure.header: Start with flowchart (or graph) and a direction: TD, TB, BT, LR or RL.
structure.statements: One statement per line, or several on a line separated by ;.
structure.comment: Everything after %% on a line is a comment.
structure.identifier: An identifier is letters, digits and _ with no spaces or hyphens: step_1.
structure.define: Write a block's form once; later mention only its identifier.
structure.quotes: Always put the text in double quotes: A["text"]. Without quotes the text ends at the first closing bracket, so a[i] or f(x) would break it. A double quote cannot be used inside the text; use ' or « » instead.
structure.breaks:
Break a line inside the quotes with
.

blocks.title: Blocks
blocks.text: Pick the block by what the step means, not by looks. In the forms below, A is any identifier. Click a form to copy it.
blocks.tip: Input or output is the general block. Use manual input only for typing, display only for a screen and document only for print.
blocks.preparation: Preparation, head of a counted loop

shapes.title: Blocks by name and properties
shapes.text: Any block can also be written as A@{ shape: name, label: "text" } with the shape names Mermaid uses (doc, sl-rect, trap-t, fork, ...); Rhumb adds seq-store, loop-start and loop-end. The same braces carry the properties of a block, also after a short form: A["text"] @{ ident: "P1" }.
shapes.warning: Give the shape once: either in brackets or in shape:, never both.

extras.ident: Identifier above the block, on the left
extras.desc: Description above the block, on the right
extras.input: Description below the block, on the right
extras.ref: Stripe that points to a detailed sheet
extras.loop: Name that joins the two loop limits
extras.side: Side of a comment: right, left, top or bottom
extras.legend: What the letter of a transfer stands for, shown under the diagram

lines.title: Lines and labels
lines.text: Longer runs such as ---> mean the same. Mermaid's --o, --x and <--> are not supported.
lines.label: Label on a line
lines.labelSpaced: The same; spaces around the text

decisions.title: Decisions and loops
decisions.branches: Label every branch of a decision, Yes and No for two exits, one value per exit for more. The profile decides which side each one leaves from; unlabeled branches use the free sides in order. Where the profile leaves the side open, a branch that goes back to a preparation block leaves on the side that block takes returning lines on.
decisions.preparation: When the flow comes back to a preparation block, the line into the repeated section leaves from the bottom, returning lines enter one side corner and the other lines leave from the opposite one. Write the line into the body first, then the exit.
decisions.limits: Loop limits are another way to draw a loop. The name before the colon joins the start to its end, so nested loops need different names. Pick one style per diagram.

frames.title: Frames and comments
frames.frame: A frame is a dashed outline around blocks: subgraph id ["Title"] ... end. The identifier is required, frames nest, a frame holds at least one block, and a block belongs to the frame it is first named in.
frames.comment: A comment is tied to a block or a frame with a dashed link, exactly one per comment, and stands beside it. It takes no label.

parallel.title: Parallel actions, transfers and sheets
parallel.bars: One bar [=] splits the flow, another joins it. Use two bars, never one for both.
parallel.transfer: A transfer of control is one letter; its meaning goes in legend and is listed under the diagram. One letter cannot stand for two meanings.
parallel.sheets: A break in a line between sheets is two connectors with the same text and different identifiers. A stripe (ref) marks a block that is drawn in detail on another sheet.

errors.title: Common errors
errors.text: An error message starts with the line to fix. These are the usual ones.
errors.unsupported: Remove classDef, class, style, linkStyle, click and direction. Rhumb has no styling.
errors.link: Something between two blocks is not a line: look for an unquoted bracket in the text, a hyphen in an identifier, or & joining blocks.
errors.quote: There is a double quote inside the text. Use ' or « » instead.
errors.shape: Use one of the shape names; see Blocks by name and properties.
errors.empty: Put at least one block in the frame.
errors.note: Tie every comment to exactly one block or frame with -.-.
errors.loop: Every loop start needs an end with the same name.
errors.type: Rhumb draws flowcharts only; start with flowchart.

standards.title: Standards
standards.text: A standard is a JSON profile with block sizes, line widths, fonts and branch sides. Pick a built-in one on the Config tab or load your own.

agents.title: For AI agents
agents.text: An AI agent can write Rhumb diagrams for you, but what it knows about Mermaid does not cover Rhumb's own blocks and rules. Give it one of these files. A skill is a folder an agent loads when it needs it; a prompt is plain text for any chat.
agents.skill: Skill: upload the .zip in the skills settings of your agent, or unpack it into its skills folder.
agents.prompt: Prompt: paste it into custom instructions, a project or a system prompt. The short one fits small context windows.
agents.link: An agent that can open links can read a file by its link.
agents.note: The files are made from the same source as this help and carry the version of the app.
